metadata.key_test: Safeguard H (centripetal classifier): does a Tier-1, very-high-P1 federation absorb a razor-thin secession near-miss (the 30 Oct 1995 'No' won by ~1.16%) peacefully and LEGALLY (1998 Supreme Court Secession Reference, 2000 Clarity Act) without violence or territorial loss? Tests that very high founding P1 predicts peaceful, lawful management of separatism REGARDLESS of how close the vote is. Quebec is a SUB-STATE province -> proxied via Canada (country_ref) + qualitative evidence; no standalone WGI/MI. NB: the 1995 referendum predates the WGI series (which starts 1996), so the pre-event is anchored to 1996 as a proxy (flagged pre-WGI).
metadata.notes: Reference-based record. Canada carries real MI v2 re-scores; Quebec is a sub-state proxy entity with no resolved scores (mirrors Aceh case35 / Catalonia case16 handling). The North-American required case; the centripetal counterpart to lower-P1 Catalonia (case16). Scored ~1996 (proxy for the 1995 referendum) vs 2024.

pre_event.event_description: The 30 October 1995 Quebec sovereignty referendum failed by the narrowest of margins -- 'No' 50.58% vs 'Yes' 49.42% (a ~1.16-point gap). The near-miss triggered not violence or suppression but a legal-constitutional response: the federal government's 1998 reference to the Supreme Court on the legality of unilateral secession, and the resulting Clarity Act (2000) setting the conditions (a clear question, a clear majority) under which Ottawa would negotiate. Because the WGI series begins in 1996, the pre-event is anchored to 1996 as a proxy for the 1995 state of the federation (flagged).

Canada.outcome_summary: Containment as predicted. The federation absorbed the 1995 near-miss with zero violence: the Supreme Court's 1998 Secession Reference and the 2000 Clarity Act converted the crisis into a durable legal-constitutional framework. No further referendum was held; sovereignty support trended down. Canada's P1 stayed Tier 1 (0.846 -> 0.797) and MI held at 0.850 -> 0.806 (Tier 1). The centripetal (Safeguard H) counterpart to lower-P1 Catalonia (case16).
key_events: 1998 Supreme Court of Canada Reference re Secession of Quebec
2000 Clarity Act (clear question + clear majority conditions)
2006 House of Commons motion recognizing 'the Quebecois as a nation within a united Canada'
Parti Quebecois decline; no further sovereignty referendum through 2024

Quebec.outcome_summary: Qualitative (sub-state, no WB data): the sovereignty option lost momentum after 1995. The PQ lost power in 2003, sovereignty support eroded, and Quebec's grievances were channeled into intergovernmental and fiscal accommodation within the federation rather than a renewed secession drive. No secession; no violence.
key_events: sovereignty support declines; no second referendum

analysis.overall_assessment: Clean confirmation expected and delivered: a Tier-1 federation absorbed a razor-thin secession near-miss with zero violence and converted it into durable legal-constitutional management. Quebec, as a sub-state proxy, is assessed qualitatively.

analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Very high founding P1 predicts peaceful, lawful containment of separatism INDEPENDENT of how close the vote is: a Tier-1 federation absorbed a 1.16-point secession near-miss with no violence and institutionalized the outcome (Clarity Act). It is the centripetal (Safeguard H) high-P1 counterpart to the lower-P1 Catalonia case (case16) -- closeness of the vote did not translate into instability where institutional quality was top-tier.
